data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resumption may proceed if and only if the event framing protocol provides deterministic delimiters that allow trailing partial bytes to be classified as non-events; resumption must be refused when framing is ambiguous and cannot distinguish a complete event from a partial fragment.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the framing protocol relies solely on external length-prefixing without end-markers or checksums, trailing bytes cannot be deterministically classified as non-events, requiring refusal of resumption.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the resumption protocol attempts to garbage-collect or rewrite the partial bytes rather than ignoring them, it modifies the append-only log and must be refused.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If no complete event was framed before exhaustion, resumption cannot anchor causal continuity and must be refused until a complete event is available.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A partial byte sequence left by mid-stream exhaustion lacks event identity under proper framing. The resumption protocol simply ignores trailing bytes after the last framed complete event. No append-only violation occurs because no committed event was deleted or modified\u2014non-events were skipped, preserving both physical append-only integrity and logical causal continuity.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
